Sowbot (ROS 2 stack)

An open-source, containerised ROS2 Jazzy stack for autonomous agricultural robotics. This repository provides the drivers and orchestration for the Sowbot platform, featuring RTK-GNSS localisation and STM32-based hardware control.

Field results

None published yet. Simulation results are not evidence for the tracked hardware (Gazebo does not model slip). Once hardware runs start, each will report: cross-track error (RMS and maximum), share of time in RTK fixed, interventions per hour, and measured stopping distance. The progression from bench to supervised rows, with exit criteria for each step, is in docs/field-validation.md.

Quick Start

Supported SBC configuration

  • Avaota A1
  • Armbian (note flash with official Armbian flasher)

0. Install dependencies

Linux

  • Git
  • Docker
  • sudo apt install python3-serial setserial v4l-utils
  • sudo apt install -y pipx && pipx install 'glances[web]' && pipx ensurepath && (nohup ~/.local/bin/glances -w --bind 127.0.0.1 > /tmp/glances.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &)

Mac

  • xcode-select --install
  • Git
  • Docker
  • & launch Gazebo in a browser from the WebUI.

Windows?

  • Git
  • Docker
  • Untested!

1. Clone the Repository

Open a terminal on your host machine and download the workspace:

git clone -b caatinga-dev https://github.com/Agroecology-Lab/Sowbot.git
cd Sowbot

2. Build & Launch

Use the management script to build the ROS 2 workspace and launch the robot stack. This script automatically handles hardware discovery and port permissions:

./manage.py full-build
xhost +local:docker
./manage.py

Access http://localhost to access the WebUI

The dashboard has a joystick and a soft e-stop and listens on port 80 of the robot. Set SOWBOT_UI_PASSWORD in .env to require a password (HTTP Basic, user name ignored). Without it, anyone on the robot's network can drive it. Basic auth is not encrypted, so also keep the robot's Wi-Fi private. The container runs privileged on the host network.

Linux

If you're getting this error:

docker: Error response from daemon: could not select device driver "" with capabilities: [[gpu]]

You'll need to install the Nvidia Container runtime.

Gazebo

If you'd like to use Gazebo then add a +sim argument to your build instruction

./manage.py full-build +sim
xhost +local:docker
./manage.py

Optical flow sensor (PMW3901 / PAA5100)

optical_flow_ros is built into the image (Dockerfile Stage 8, pinned by OPTICAL_FLOW_ROS_COMMIT). Its pip dependencies (pmw3901, gpiod, gpiodevice) are installed at pinned versions in Stage 5.2b.

Run inside the container:

ros2 launch devkit_bringup optical_flow.launch.py

Do not use upstream's optical_flow_launch.py: it broadcasts odom -> base_link, which FusionCore owns.

  • Sensor parameters: config/sensor_params.yaml in the upstream package (board, spi_nr, spi_slot, rotation, z_height, sensor_timeout). src/devkit_bringup/config/optical_flow.yaml is loaded after it and sets publish_tf: false. Put local driver settings there, not in the cloned source.
  • The launch remaps odom to flow_odom and publishes /diagnostics.
  • flow_odom is not consumed by FusionCore (its inputs are hardcoded to /gnss/fix and /odom/wheels).
  • Upstream tested on Raspberry Pi (SPI). Not tested here on the supported SBCs.
  • Requires /dev/spidev* on the host; the container runs privileged with /dev mounted.

Known limitations of the pinned driver, not fixed here:

  • flow_odom is not fit for fusion. The orientation is left unset (0, 0, 0, 0), every covariance is zero and angular velocity is zero. Do not feed it to an estimator without fixing the message.
  • /diagnostics reports OK whenever the node runs. A sensor timeout is published as zero motion, so it is not a health signal.
  • Each read can block for up to sensor_timeout (0.5 s) inside a 100 Hz timer. A stationary sensor therefore publishes slower than 100 Hz, and the linear velocity (distance divided by the nominal 0.01 s) is wrong whenever a callback runs late.

Management & Tools

manage.py

The primary entry point for the system. While it runs the full stack by default, it supports several optional arguments for development:

Command Logic / Argument Resulting Action
./manage.py (No arguments) Runs run_runtime() immediately using live volumes.
./manage.py build build local-only, fully cached including external clones
./manage.py build +pull build Re-clones the 10 external repos, keeps apt/pip/local layers cached
./manage.py build +pull +sim build Same, plus INSTALL_SIM=true
./manage.py full-build full-build Runs run_build(full=True). Cleans system & Re-installs all system dependencies.
./manage.py neo neo Runs neo. Runs only the line following code for the second 'neo'(cortex) perception SBC. Then check http://localhost:8081 (web_video_server; 8080 is the Medkit gateway)
./manage.py neo-tsm neo-tsm Runs neo-tsm. Runs experimental line following informed by Vision based Crop Row Navigation under Varying Field Conditions in Arable Fields - Rajitha de Silva1, Grzegorz Cielniak2 and Junfeng Gao. Then check http://localhost:8081 (web_video_server; 8080 is the Medkit gateway)
./manage.py pull-caatinga pulls & builds vision pipeline Requires the container to already be running

One-command sim launch (TMuLE)

The simulation launch accepts use_camera:=false to disable the simulated camera:

ros2 launch devkit_bringup sowbot_sim.launch.py use_camera:=false

Use camera_width, camera_height, and camera_rate to override the default 320×240 image at 10 Hz. These arguments also work with ros2 launch devkit_simulation sim.launch.py.

Whilst you can launch Gazebo and other tools from the webui, some may prefer the terminal, this makes terminal use a bit easier.

TMuLE brings the whole row-following sim up in a single tmux session — one window per process — instead of running the three launch steps by hand in separate terminals:

tmule -c tmule/row_follow_sim.yaml launch
tmux attach -t row_follow_sim

That starts ./manage.py --sim (nav stack + Nav2 + UI), Gazebo (sowbot_sim.launch.py) and the crop-row CV node (crop_row_nav.launch.py), each in its own tmux window. launch returns immediately and leaves the session detached, so attach to watch the panes come up (and to type the nav_stack sudo password).

Stop the stack with tmule -c tmule/row_follow_sim.yaml stop; re-attach later with tmux attach -t row_follow_sim.

If a runtime container is already running, the nav_stack window will fail on a docker run name collision. Either docker stop sowbot_runtime first, or launch just the windows that reuse the container: tmule -c tmule/row_follow_sim.yaml launch -w gazebo.

tmux basics

The stack runs in a detached tmux session named row_follow_sim, so closing your terminal does not kill it — detaching is not stopping. The session holds one window per sub-system (plus a stray 0: bash that tmux always creates):

0: bash   1: nav_stack   2: gazebo   3: crop_row

Every shortcut starts with the prefix Ctrl-b — press and release it, then the next key:

Keys Resulting Action
Ctrl-b d Detach — leaves the whole stack running in the background
Ctrl-b w Interactive window picker (easiest way to move around)
Ctrl-b 1 / 2 / 3 Jump straight to nav_stack / gazebo / crop_row
Ctrl-b n / p Next / previous window
Ctrl-b [ Scroll back through ROS log output — arrows/PgUp, q to exit
Ctrl-b z Zoom the current pane fullscreen (press again to unzoom)
Ctrl-b ? List every binding 
tmux ls                              # list sessions
tmux attach -t row_follow_sim        # attach
tmux kill-session -t row_follow_sim  # nuke the session

Scrolling back (Ctrl-b [) is the one you'll reach for most — it's how you read ROS output that has already scrolled past. For mouse-wheel scrolling instead, add set -g mouse on to ~/.tmux.conf.

Scenario configs live in tmule/ — see tmule/README.md to tweak launch arguments or add your own scenario.

Interactive Shell

To enter the running container for debugging or manual ROS 2 commands:

./tools/login.sh

Diagnostics

If hardware is connected but topics are not flowing, run the diagnostic tool from inside the container:

After running ./tools/login.sh

python3 tools/agbot-diagnostic.py

You can also make it verbose with:

python3 tools/agbot-diagnostic.py full

Sketch of MVP 2026 architecture

1. The Flight Controller (RT Microcontroller)

  • Hardware: LEVIA-H7 (STM32H743). Unvalidated, in bring-up.
  • Software: ArduPilot Rover, GUIDED mode.
  • Role: Motion execution and supervisory failsafes (geofence, GCS/GPS loss, EKF variance).
  • I/O: MAVLink serial from the Limbic SBC via devkit_mavlink_bridge; CAN for motor drivers (driver choice open).
  • Not the rated stop function. Stopping on a bumper, radar or E-stop is done by the hardwired 24V loop, independent of this controller (see safety_roadmap.md).
  • Legacy: ESP32 + Lizard DSL (3.3V UART via the teleop_lizard bridge, see docs/lizard-firmware-setup.md). Kept for existing hardware, no new features.

2. The Limbic System (Executive)

  • Hardware: Avaota A1 #1 (Allwinner T527).
  • Software: ROS 2 Jazzy + topological_navigation (main).
  • Role: Navigation Executive.
  • Function: Runs the Nav2-based Topological Navigation stack. Manages NavigateToPose actions and Action on Condition (AOC) logic.
  • I/O: Connects to u-blox via USB/UART using ublox_dgnss node. Translates graph goals into velocity commands for the flight controller.

<1GbE interconnect between 2&3>

3. The Neo (Perception)

  • Hardware: Avaota A1 #2 (Allwinner T527 + NPU).

  • Software: Dockerised ROS 2 Jazzy.

  • Role: Asynchronous Perception.

  • Function: NPU-accelerated inference (YOLO/Object tracking) and sensor fusion.

  • Connectivity: Native Zenoh integration via rmw_zenoh_cpp. Publishes environment states and "Conditions" to the Zenoh network.

                        |

Sketch of possible eventual ~2027 architecture

Research only (TRL 1 to 2 in the roadmap above), not a commitment. It would replace ArduPilot on the controller, which is the current path.

1. The Real-Time Controller (Hardware Abstraction)

  • Hardware: STM32 H7 MCU.
  • Software: copper-rs.
  • Role: Hard Real-Time Execution.
  • Function: Manages motor PID loops and hardware-level safety interlocks.
  • I/O: Canbus

2. The Limbic System (Executive)

  • Hardware: Avaota A1 #1 (Allwinner T527).
  • Software: RT kernel, Buildroot copper-rs
  • Role: Deterministic Executive.
  • Function: UBLOX sensors, Executes Action on Condition (AOC) logic for topological navigation.
  • Data Entry: Directly consumes Zenoh keys from the Neo board to trigger mission state transitions and motion planning.
Core(s) Role Allocation Strategy
Core 0 OS / I/O Handles kernel house-keeping, SSH, and the 1GbE driver interrupts.
Core 1 Zenoh / Neo-link Dedicated to the Zenoh router and serializing incoming "Nice-to-Have" data.
Cores 2-6 The Pilot (Nav) This is where the RTK EKF, Path Planner, and Task Graph live.
Core 7 The Bridge (controller) Dedicated to SocketCAN and the high-frequency heartbeat to the STM32.

<1GbE interconnect between 2&3>

3. The Neo (Perception)

  • Hardware: Avaota A1 #2 (Allwinner T527 + NPU).
  • Software: Dockerised ROS 2 Jazzy & Dockerised CV packages
  • Role: Asynchronous Perception.
  • Function: NPU-accelerated inference (YOLO/Object tracking) and sensor fusion.
  • Connectivity: Native Zenoh integration via rmw_zenoh_cpp. Publishes environment states and "Conditions" to the Zenoh network.

content_text: Sowbot (ROS 2 stack) An open-source, containerised ROS2 Jazzy stack for autonomous agricultural robotics. This repository provides the drivers and orchestration for the Sowbot platform, featuring RTK-GNSS localisation and STM32-based hardware control. Live volume mapping to /workspace. Build, full-build, and +sim build modes. Done 6 2025 F2 Stable device addressing tools/fixusb.py with Jetson/generic architecture detection, kernel low_latency mode, and udev symlink generation. Writes .env consumed by all launch files. Note: run_neo() never calls tools/fixusb.py so .env is not written for neo-only runs. Done 6 2025 F3 Teleop dashboard NiceGUI web cockpit on :80. Four tabs: Run, Plan, Sim, System. Joystick, e-stop, topo map, node-drop, track mode, fields2cover corner entry, F2C row plan generator, reorderable mission queue, telemetry, safety indicators, GPS leaflet map. LiteFarm GeoJSON export on System, Tools card (M11). Done 6 2025 F4 ublox DGNSS driver Dual F9P moving-base configuration with dynamic port assignment via tools/fixusb.py. Done 6 2026 F5 Diagnostics TUI tools/agbot-diagnostic.py terminal status view of all hardware topics. Run inside container via tools/login.sh. Done 6 2025 MVP FIELD 2026 M1 Agri Open Core platform integration Demonstrates AOC platform abstraction on affordable ARM hardware accessible to smallholders. Done 3 2026 M2 Topological navigation + Nav2 LCAS topological_navigation at a commit pinned in the Dockerfile, building in Docker. RViz visualisation confirmed working. Self-contained navigation2.py with A* route planning, explicit state machine, and row_traversal / NavigateToPose / goal_align edge actions. fake_nav2_server with /limbic_row_follow stub enables full pipeline testing in sim. sim_nav.launch.py now routes through real Nav2. Multi-row mission following (entry/exit node pairs across boustrophedon rows) validated end-to-end in Gazebo. Pending: Jazzy field validation on hardware. Sim only. Blocked: hardware field validation 4 2026 M2a fusioncore Nav2 bridge fusioncore_node launched via devkit.launch.py when the MAVLink bridge is not running; with the bridge, EKF3 is the estimator and FusionCore is shadow only (M9). Nav2 topic remapping shim wired. Pending: end-to-end test on live hardware. Blocked: live hardware test 4 2026 M3 Open-field row-crop scenario Live node-drop in UI. F2C row plan generator implemented in PlanApplicationService (corners → swaths → topo rows via run_f2c()). F2C planner clips swaths against the obstacle list. YAML written to /workspace/maps/, switch_topological_map with fallback. Topo map auto-generated at container start. Multi-row traversal across generated swaths confirmed in sim. Web version of planner available Pending: tmap2 authoring from real field survey; obstacle costmap layer (obstacles are published on /obstacles but no costmap consumes them). Sim only. Blocked: real-field tmap2 survey, obstacle costmap layer 4 2026 M4 RTK-GNSS localisation Full pipeline implemented: dual F9P, shims, UKF fusion, NTRIP. Lever-arm offsets in fusioncore.yaml are zeroed placeholders (commented # measured TODOs); manage.py exits 1 at startup unless ALLOW_UNMEASURED_LEVER_ARM=1. Pending: antenna lever-arm measurement, live hardware test. Do not quote accuracy before the lever arms are measured. Blocked: lever-arm measurement, live hardware test 3 2026 M5 Dual-SBC ROS 2 stack manage.py detects crossover interface, builds CYCLONEDDS_URI peer config and injects into Docker. neo.launch.py and devkit.launch.py finalised for Limbic+Neo split. DDS peer path is the active one. Implemented. No hardware test recorded 3 2026 M6 Gazebo simulation sowbot_sim.launch.py + sim_nav.launch.py fully restructured. kill_fake_nav2_on_clock implemented. use_sim_time=True now threaded through topo stack. Gazebo does not model track slip, so these results do not carry over to the tracked hardware. Multi-row mission following demonstrated end-to-end (see video above). Done 4 2026 M7 Sentor safety monitoring sowbot_monitor.yaml fully authored (e-stop, bumpers, battery, camera, odom, neo_vision heartbeat, node monitors). sentor_node.py wired into devkit.launch.py. Pending: smoke-test on live hardware; battery voltage cutoff needs field confirmation (# TODO: CONFIRM in YAML). GNSS fix and heading monitors report only; no response is defined yet. Blocked: hardware smoke test, battery cutoff 3 2026 M8 Visual crop-row navigation sowbot_row_follow package implemented. ExG+Otsu, visual servo, limbic_row_follow_node.py as Nav2 action server. Cancel and heartbeat-loss safety. TSM row-swap hold with 6-second debounce implemented. Tested and iterated against a lettuce crop in the UK. Tested on lettuce. No metrics published 4 2026 M9 ArduPilot on LEVIA-H7 controller path Replaces ESP32/Lizard. devkit_mavlink_bridge commands zero when cmd_vel is stale and publishes EKF3 state and GPS status (fc/odom, fc/ekf_fix, fc/gps1/fix, fc/gps2/fix, fc/diagnostics); unit-tested against doubles, not yet run against a flight controller. EKF3 is the sole estimator and FusionCore is shadow only (src/devkit_mavlink_bridge/mavlink.md). LEVIA-H7 is unvalidated and has no confirmed ArduPilot hwdef (safety_roadmap.md O31). WIP, bring-up 2 2026 M10 MeshCore robot-to-robot avoidance src/devkit-meshcore-avoid (sowbot_avoid). Simulation only; never run on hardware. Not a safety function. Not referenced by the Docker build, manage.py or the launch files. Sim only. Blocked: hardware test, integration 2 2026 M11 LiteFarm interface (optional) Imports a LiteFarm farm map (rows, docks, routes; content_hash checked, hash8 stamped into the topo map). Exports row plans as GeoJSON (System tab, Tools card; row_plan_cli). row_plan_cli --import-to POSTs to /row_plan/import; no UI button for the POST. Format: docs/row-plan-geojson.md. Implemented, optional. Unit-tested without hardware 3 2026 M12 Remote missions Mission store and spec (missions.md). No intake, radio link or base station; add_remote has no callers. Partial, spec only 2 2026 PRODUCTION ~2027 P1 Phase 1: dev platform (current) Controller: ArduPilot on LEVIA-H7 (M9); ESP32/Lizard is legacy. Supervised-only until the 24V stop loop, radar validation and beacon are done (safety_roadmap.md O7, O8, O14). Audience: university labs, ag-tech researchers, software startups. No compliance claimed, standards used as informal design reference only, user's own risk per README. Product classification depends on the shipped configuration and incorporation boundary (O16); complete machinery requires conformity assessment, documentation and applicable marking. In progress. Blocked: O7, O8, O14; shipment blocked on O16 4 2026 P2 Phase 2: OEM modular subsystems Packages the Phase 1 stack (Ardupilot on Levia STM32 H7, M9) for integrators. Audience: startups integrating Sowbot's core. No third-party certification needed yet, formal internal assessment only. Can offer PLd hardware subsystem Research 2 2027 P3 Phase 3: commercial sale to farmers (Safety sub-systems hardened) Full ISO 18497 compliance, ISO 13849 PLc certification (or equivalent), third-party safety audit, field trial history, and an insurance/liability structure. All required before sale, none yet scoped. Planned 1 2027+ P4 CANopen bus ISO 11898 FDCAN at 500 kbit/s / 2 Mbit/s. lely-core CANopen master on T527 native M_CAN. DSP402 drive profile. Research 2 2027 P5 RT kernel + core isolation PREEMPT_RT on Limbic T527. isolcpus=4-7, RTK EKF on core 2 (SCHED_FIFO 60), AOC nav on cores 4-6, watchdog on core 5. GbE/CAN IRQ pinned to core 0. Planned 2 2027 P6 ROFS image Read-only rootfs, Ubuntu Noble minimal or Yocto with RT kernel, pre-built LCAS topo nav, Nav2, rmw_zenoh_cpp (the current stack uses rmw_cyclonedds_cpp, M5). Immutable field deployment. Research 1 2027 END-EFFECTORS TBD E1 Delta weeding module Open-Weeding-Delta precision mechanical weeding. CANopen actuator node on delta controller. Research 1 TBD E2 LASER weeding module Laudando LASER integration. Requires E-Stop interlocking with CANopen safety chain. Research 1 TBD DATASETS & COLLABORATION Ongoing D1 UK open-field dataset Field imagery and GNSS logs from UK agroecological farm conditions. CC licence. Planned 2 2026 D2 Caatinga biome dataset Semi-arid row-crop imagery from caatingarobotics. Validated on T527 AIPU. Active 5 2026 TRL = Technology Readiness Level (1–9, ESA/NASA scale): 1–2 concept/formulation, 3 proof of concept, 4 validated in lab/simulation, 5 validated in relevant (non-lab) environment, 6 demonstrated in relevant environment, 7 operational prototype, 8 qualified system, 9 field-proven. Self-assessed per feature, not a formal review — adjust as needed. Field results None published yet. Simulation results are not evidence for the tracked hardware (Gazebo does not model slip). Once hardware runs start, each will report: cross-track error (RMS and maximum), share of time in RTK fixed, interventions per hour, and measured stopping distance. The progression from bench to supervised rows, with exit criteria for each step, is in docs/field-validation.md. Collaboration This project is built on and aims to maintain upstream compatibility with zauberzeug/feldfreund_devkit_ros. High Level navigation is developed from the work of Lincoln Centre for Autonomous Systems (LCAS) as part of the Agri-OpenCore open ROS 2 ecosystem for agricultural robotic Simulation configuration is partially derived from work by caatingarobotics, ⚠️ CRITICAL SAFETY WARNING: This software is under active development and may be broken at any given moment. For a stable reference implementation see the upstream Zauberzeug project. THIS SOFTWARE COULD CONTROL PHYSICAL HARDWARE CAPABLE OF PRODUCING SIGNIFICANT KINETIC FORCE. EXPERIMENTAL STATUS: This branch ('caatinga-dev') contains experimental code generated and refined with AI assistance. It has NOT undergone full-scale field validation. STATUTORY NOTICE (UK): Usage of this software is at the user's sole risk. While standard open-source licenses apply, users are reminded that operating agricultural robotics requires a professional duty of care. MANDATORY HARDWARE SAFETY: Under no circumstances should this software be used to control a robot of any size without an independent safety subsystem. Software-based stops (such as /estop/soft) are NOT a substitute for Category 0 or 1 hardware safety stops. CURRENT STATUS: the hardwired 24V stop loop is still being built and the radar is not yet validated on the vehicle (see safety_roadmap.md, O7, O8, O14). Operation requires the hard-wired 24V loop, including the physical E-stop path, to be built and tested, or a separately validated independent stop method; otherwise operation is prohibited. Until O7, O8 and O14 close, any permitted operation is supervised-only, with a competent person within reach of a physical E-stop (or the separately validated stop control), nobody working near it, and no safety claim made. NO LIABILITY: To the extent permitted by the laws of England and Wales, the contributors exclude all liability for property damage, crop loss, or indirect consequential damages. Health Warning This repo may contain traces of LLM slop. We've done our best to mitigate this. If you are allergic to slop, please help us refactor. Quick Start Supported SBC configuration Avaota A1 Armbian (note flash with official Armbian flasher) 0. Install dependencies Linux Git Docker sudo apt install python3-serial setserial v4l-utils sudo apt install -y pipx && pipx install 'glances[web]' && pipx ensurepath && (nohup ~/.local/bin/glances -w --bind 127.0.0.1 > /tmp/glances.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &) Mac xcode-select --install Git Docker & launch Gazebo in a browser from the WebUI. Windows? Git Docker Untested! 1. Clone the Repository Open a terminal on your host machine and download the workspace: git clone -b caatinga-dev https://github.com/Agroecology-Lab/Sowbot.git cd Sowbot 2. Build & Launch Use the management script to build the ROS 2 workspace and launch the robot stack. This script automatically handles hardware discovery and port permissions: ./manage.py full-build xhost +local:docker ./manage.py Access http://localhost to access the WebUI The dashboard has a joystick and a soft e-stop and listens on port 80 of the robot. Set SOWBOT_UI_PASSWORD in .env to require a password (HTTP Basic, user name ignored). Without it, anyone on the robot's network can drive it. Basic auth is not encrypted, so also keep the robot's Wi-Fi private. The container runs privileged on the host network. Linux If you're getting this error: docker: Error response from daemon: could not select device driver "" with capabilities: [[gpu]] You'll need to install the Nvidia Container runtime. Gazebo If you'd like to use Gazebo then add a +sim argument to your build instruction ./manage.py full-build +sim xhost +local:docker ./manage.py Optical flow sensor (PMW3901 / PAA5100) optical_flow_ros is built into the image (Dockerfile Stage 8, pinned by OPTICAL_FLOW_ROS_COMMIT). Its pip dependencies (pmw3901, gpiod, gpiodevice) are installed at pinned versions in Stage 5.2b. Run inside the container: ros2 launch devkit_bringup optical_flow.launch.py Do not use upstream's optical_flow_launch.py: it broadcasts odom -> base_link, which FusionCore owns. Sensor parameters: config/sensor_params.yaml in the upstream package (board, spi_nr, spi_slot, rotation, z_height, sensor_timeout). src/devkit_bringup/config/optical_flow.yaml is loaded after it and sets publish_tf: false. Put local driver settings there, not in the cloned source. The launch remaps odom to flow_odom and publishes /diagnostics. flow_odom is not consumed by FusionCore (its inputs are hardcoded to /gnss/fix and /odom/wheels). Upstream tested on Raspberry Pi (SPI). Not tested here on the supported SBCs. Requires /dev/spidev* on the host; the container runs privileged with /dev mounted. Known limitations of the pinned driver, not fixed here: flow_odom is not fit for fusion. The orientation is left unset (0, 0, 0, 0), every covariance is zero and angular velocity is zero. Do not feed it to an estimator without fixing the message. /diagnostics reports OK whenever the node runs. A sensor timeout is published as zero motion, so it is not a health signal. Each read can block for up to sensor_timeout (0.5 s) inside a 100 Hz timer. A stationary sensor therefore publishes slower than 100 Hz, and the linear velocity (distance divided by the nominal 0.01 s) is wrong whenever a callback runs late. Management & Tools manage.py The primary entry point for the system. While it runs the full stack by default, it supports several optional arguments for development: Command Logic / Argument Resulting Action ./manage.py (No arguments) Runs run_runtime() immediately using live volumes. ./manage.py build build local-only, fully cached including external clones ./manage.py build +pull build Re-clones the 10 external repos, keeps apt/pip/local layers cached ./manage.py build +pull +sim build Same, plus INSTALL_SIM=true ./manage.py full-build full-build Runs run_build(full=True). Cleans system & Re-installs all system dependencies. ./manage.py neo neo Runs neo. Runs only the line following code for the second 'neo'(cortex) perception SBC. Then check http://localhost:8081 (web_video_server; 8080 is the Medkit gateway) ./manage.py neo-tsm neo-tsm Runs neo-tsm. Runs experimental line following informed by Vision based Crop Row Navigation under Varying Field Conditions in Arable Fields - Rajitha de Silva1, Grzegorz Cielniak2 and Junfeng Gao. Then check http://localhost:8081 (web_video_server; 8080 is the Medkit gateway) ./manage.py pull-caatinga pulls & builds vision pipeline Requires the container to already be running One-command sim launch (TMuLE) The simulation launch accepts use_camera:=false to disable the simulated camera: ros2 launch devkit_bringup sowbot_sim.launch.py use_camera:=false Use camera_width, camera_height, and camera_rate to override the default 320×240 image at 10 Hz. These arguments also work with ros2 launch devkit_simulation sim.launch.py. Whilst you can launch Gazebo and other tools from the webui, some may prefer the terminal, this makes terminal use a bit easier. TMuLE brings the whole row-following sim up in a single tmux session — one window per process — instead of running the three launch steps by hand in separate terminals: tmule -c tmule/row_follow_sim.yaml launch tmux attach -t row_follow_sim That starts ./manage.py --sim (nav stack + Nav2 + UI), Gazebo (sowbot_sim.launch.py) and the crop-row CV node (crop_row_nav.launch.py), each in its own tmux window. launch returns immediately and leaves the session detached, so attach to watch the panes come up (and to type the nav_stack sudo password). Stop the stack with tmule -c tmule/row_follow_sim.yaml stop; re-attach later with tmux attach -t row_follow_sim. If a runtime container is already running, the nav_stack window will fail on a docker run name collision. Either docker stop sowbot_runtime first, or launch just the windows that reuse the container: tmule -c tmule/row_follow_sim.yaml launch -w gazebo. tmux basics The stack runs in a detached tmux session named row_follow_sim, so closing your terminal does not kill it — detaching is not stopping. The session holds one window per sub-system (plus a stray 0: bash that tmux always creates): 0: bash 1: nav_stack 2: gazebo 3: crop_row Every shortcut starts with the prefix Ctrl-b — press and release it, then the next key: Keys Resulting Action Ctrl-b d Detach — leaves the whole stack running in the background Ctrl-b w Interactive window picker (easiest way to move around) Ctrl-b 1 / 2 / 3 Jump straight to nav_stack / gazebo / crop_row Ctrl-b n / p Next / previous window Ctrl-b [ Scroll back through ROS log output — arrows/PgUp, q to exit Ctrl-b z Zoom the current pane fullscreen (press again to unzoom) Ctrl-b ? List every binding tmux ls # list sessions tmux attach -t row_follow_sim # attach tmux kill-session -t row_follow_sim # nuke the session Scrolling back (Ctrl-b [) is the one you'll reach for most — it's how you read ROS output that has already scrolled past. For mouse-wheel scrolling instead, add set -g mouse on to ~/.tmux.conf. Scenario configs live in tmule/ — see tmule/README.md to tweak launch arguments or add your own scenario. Interactive Shell To enter the running container for debugging or manual ROS 2 commands: ./tools/login.sh Diagnostics If hardware is connected but topics are not flowing, run the diagnostic tool from inside the container: After running ./tools/login.sh python3 tools/agbot-diagnostic.py You can also make it verbose with: python3 tools/agbot-diagnostic.py full Sketch of MVP 2026 architecture 1. The Flight Controller (RT Microcontroller) Hardware: LEVIA-H7 (STM32H743). Unvalidated, in bring-up. Software: ArduPilot Rover, GUIDED mode. Role: Motion execution and supervisory failsafes (geofence, GCS/GPS loss, EKF variance). I/O: MAVLink serial from the Limbic SBC via devkit_mavlink_bridge; CAN for motor drivers (driver choice open). Not the rated stop function. Stopping on a bumper, radar or E-stop is done by the hardwired 24V loop, independent of this controller (see safety_roadmap.md). Legacy: ESP32 + Lizard DSL (3.3V UART via the teleop_lizard bridge, see docs/lizard-firmware-setup.md). Kept for existing hardware, no new features. 2. The Limbic System (Executive) Hardware: Avaota A1 #1 (Allwinner T527). Software: ROS 2 Jazzy + topological_navigation (main). Role: Navigation Executive. Function: Runs the Nav2-based Topological Navigation stack. Manages NavigateToPose actions and Action on Condition (AOC) logic. I/O: Connects to u-blox via USB/UART using ublox_dgnss node. Translates graph goals into velocity commands for the flight controller. <1GbE interconnect between 2&3> 3. The Neo (Perception) Hardware: Avaota A1 #2 (Allwinner T527 + NPU). Software: Dockerised ROS 2 Jazzy. Role: Asynchronous Perception. Function: NPU-accelerated inference (YOLO/Object tracking) and sensor fusion. Connectivity: Native Zenoh integration via rmw_zenoh_cpp. Publishes environment states and "Conditions" to the Zenoh network. | Sketch of possible eventual ~2027 architecture Research only (TRL 1 to 2 in the roadmap above), not a commitment. It would replace ArduPilot on the controller, which is the current path. 1. The Real-Time Controller (Hardware Abstraction) Hardware: STM32 H7 MCU. Software: copper-rs. Role: Hard Real-Time Execution. Function: Manages motor PID loops and hardware-level safety interlocks. I/O: Canbus 2. The Limbic System (Executive) Hardware: Avaota A1 #1 (Allwinner T527). Software: RT kernel, Buildroot copper-rs Role: Deterministic Executive. Function: UBLOX sensors, Executes Action on Condition (AOC) logic for topological navigation. Data Entry: Directly consumes Zenoh keys from the Neo board to trigger mission state transitions and motion planning. Core(s) Role Allocation Strategy Core 0 OS / I/O Handles kernel house-keeping, SSH, and the 1GbE driver interrupts. Core 1 Zenoh / Neo-link Dedicated to the Zenoh router and serializing incoming "Nice-to-Have" data. Cores 2-6 The Pilot (Nav) This is where the RTK EKF, Path Planner, and Task Graph live. Core 7 The Bridge (controller) Dedicated to SocketCAN and the high-frequency heartbeat to the STM32. <1GbE interconnect between 2&3> 3. The Neo (Perception) Hardware: Avaota A1 #2 (Allwinner T527 + NPU). Software: Dockerised ROS 2 Jazzy & Dockerised CV packages Role: Asynchronous Perception. Function: NPU-accelerated inference (YOLO/Object tracking) and sensor fusion. Connectivity: Native Zenoh integration via rmw_zenoh_cpp. Publishes environment states and "Conditions" to the Zenoh network. An open-source, containerised ROS2 Jazzy stack for autonomous agricultural robotics. This repository provides the drivers and orchestration for the Sowbot platform, featuring RTK-GNSS localisation and STM32-based hardware control.

1. 克隆存储库

Open a terminal on your host machine and download the workspace:

git clone -b caatinga-dev https://github.com/Agroecology-Lab/Sowbot.git
cd Sowbot

2. Build & Launch

Use the management script to build the ROS 2 workspace and launch the robot stack. This script automatically handles hardware discovery and port permissions:

./manage.py full-build
xhost +local:docker
./manage.py

Access http://localhost to access the WebUI

The dashboard has a joystick and a soft e-stop and listens on port 80 of the robot. Set SOWBOT_UI_PASSWORD in .env to require a password (HTTP Basic, user name ignored). Without it, anyone on the robot's network can drive it. Basic auth is not encrypted, so also keep the robot's Wi-Fi private. The container runs privileged on the host network.

Linux

If you're getting this error:

docker: Error response from daemon: could not select device driver "" with capabilities: [[gpu]]

You'll need to install the Nvidia Container runtime.

Gazebo

If you'd like to use Gazebo then add a +sim argument to your build instruction

./manage.py full-build +sim
xhost +local:docker
./manage.py

Optical flow sensor (PMW3901 / PAA5100)

optical_flow_ros is built into the image (Dockerfile Stage 8, pinned by OPTICAL_FLOW_ROS_COMMIT). Its pip dependencies (pmw3901, gpiod, gpiodevice) are installed at pinned versions in Stage 5.2b.

Run inside the container:

ros2 launch devkit_bringup optical_flow.launch.py

Do not use upstream's optical_flow_launch.py: it broadcasts odom -> base_link, which FusionCore owns.

  • Sensor parameters: config/sensor_params.yaml in the upstream package (board, spi_nr, spi_slot, rotation, z_height, sensor_timeout). src/devkit_bringup/config/optical_flow.yaml is loaded after it and sets publish_tf: false. Put local driver settings there, not in the cloned source.
  • The launch remaps odom to flow_odom and publishes /diagnostics.
  • flow_odom is not consumed by FusionCore (its inputs are hardcoded to /gnss/fix and /odom/wheels).
  • Upstream tested on Raspberry Pi (SPI). Not tested here on the supported SBCs.
  • Requires /dev/spidev* on the host; the container runs privileged with /dev mounted.

Known limitations of the pinned driver, not fixed here:

  • flow_odom is not fit for fusion. The orientation is left unset (0, 0, 0, 0), every covariance is zero and angular velocity is zero. Do not feed it to an estimator without fixing the message.
  • /diagnostics reports OK whenever the node runs. A sensor timeout is published as zero motion, so it is not a health signal.
  • Each read can block for up to sensor_timeout (0.5 s) inside a 100 Hz timer. A stationary sensor therefore publishes slower than 100 Hz, and the linear velocity (distance divided by the nominal 0.01 s) is wrong whenever a callback runs late.

Management & Tools

manage.py

The primary entry point for the system. While it runs the full stack by default, it supports several optional arguments for development:

命令 Logic / Argument Resulting Action
./manage.py (No arguments) Runs run_runtime() immediately using live volumes.
./manage.py build build local-only, fully cached including external clones
./manage.py build +pull build Re-clones the 10 external repos, keeps apt/pip/local layers cached
./manage.py build +pull +sim build Same, plus INSTALL_SIM=true
./manage.py full-build full-build Runs run_build(full=True). Cleans system & Re-installs all system dependencies.
./manage.py neo neo Runs neo. Runs only the line following code for the second 'neo'(cortex) perception SBC. Then check http://localhost:8081 (web_video_server; 8080 is the Medkit gateway)
./manage.py neo-tsm neo-tsm Runs neo-tsm. Runs experimental line following informed by Vision based Crop Row Navigation under Varying Field Conditions in Arable Fields - Rajitha de Silva1, Grzegorz Cielniak2 and Junfeng Gao. Then check http://localhost:8081 (web_video_server; 8080 is the Medkit gateway)
./manage.py pull-caatinga pulls & builds vision pipeline Requires the container to already be running

One-command sim launch (TMuLE)

The simulation launch accepts use_camera:=false to disable the simulated camera:

ros2 launch devkit_bringup sowbot_sim.launch.py use_camera:=false

Use camera_width, camera_height, and camera_rate to override the default 320×240 image at 10 Hz. These arguments also work with ros2 launch devkit_simulation sim.launch.py.

Whilst you can launch Gazebo and other tools from the webui, some may prefer the terminal, this makes terminal use a bit easier.

TMuLE brings the whole row-following sim up in a single tmux session — one window per process — instead of running the three launch steps by hand in separate terminals:

tmule -c tmule/row_follow_sim.yaml launch
tmux attach -t row_follow_sim

That starts ./manage.py --sim (nav stack + Nav2 + UI), Gazebo (sowbot_sim.launch.py) and the crop-row CV node (crop_row_nav.launch.py), each in its own tmux window. launch returns immediately and leaves the session detached, so attach to watch the panes come up (and to type the nav_stack sudo password).

Stop the stack with tmule -c tmule/row_follow_sim.yaml stop; re-attach later with tmux attach -t row_follow_sim.

If a runtime container is already running, the nav_stack window will fail on a docker run name collision. Either docker stop sowbot_runtime first, or launch just the windows that reuse the container: tmule -c tmule/row_follow_sim.yaml launch -w gazebo.

tmux basics

The stack runs in a detached tmux session named row_follow_sim, so closing your terminal does not kill it — detaching is not stopping. The session holds one window per sub-system (plus a stray 0: bash that tmux always creates):

0: bash   1: nav_stack   2: gazebo   3: crop_row

Every shortcut starts with the prefix Ctrl-b — press and release it, then the next key:

Keys Resulting Action
Ctrl-b d Detach — leaves the whole stack running in the background
Ctrl-b w Interactive window picker (easiest way to move around)
Ctrl-b 1 / 2 / 3 Jump straight to nav_stack / gazebo / crop_row
Ctrl-b n / p Next / previous window
Ctrl-b [ Scroll back through ROS log output — arrows/PgUp, q to exit
Ctrl-b z Zoom the current pane fullscreen (press again to unzoom)
Ctrl-b ? List every binding 
tmux ls                              # list sessions
tmux attach -t row_follow_sim        # attach
tmux kill-session -t row_follow_sim  # nuke the session

Scrolling back (Ctrl-b [) is the one you'll reach for most — it's how you read ROS output that has already scrolled past. For mouse-wheel scrolling instead, add set -g mouse on to ~/.tmux.conf.

Scenario configs live in tmule/ — see tmule/README.md to tweak launch arguments or add your own scenario.

Sketch of MVP 2026 architecture

1. The Flight Controller (RT Microcontroller)

  • Hardware: LEVIA-H7 (STM32H743). Unvalidated, in bring-up.
  • Software: ArduPilot Rover, GUIDED mode.
  • Role: Motion execution and supervisory failsafes (geofence, GCS/GPS loss, EKF variance).
  • I/O: MAVLink serial from the Limbic SBC via devkit_mavlink_bridge; CAN for motor drivers (driver choice open).
  • Not the rated stop function. Stopping on a bumper, radar or E-stop is done by the hardwired 24V loop, independent of this controller (see safety_roadmap.md).
  • Legacy: ESP32 + Lizard DSL (3.3V UART via the teleop_lizard bridge, see docs/lizard-firmware-setup.md). Kept for existing hardware, no new features.

2. The Limbic System (Executive)

  • Hardware: Avaota A1 #1 (Allwinner T527).
  • Software: ROS 2 Jazzy + topological_navigation (main).
  • Role: Navigation Executive.
  • Function: Runs the Nav2-based Topological Navigation stack. Manages NavigateToPose actions and Action on Condition (AOC) logic.
  • I/O: Connects to u-blox via USB/UART using ublox_dgnss node. Translates graph goals into velocity commands for the flight controller.
